title: Eight parked machines cost more than eight working ones
ask: The sim benchmark's scaling run measures eight idle shoo bots at about 232 microseconds a tick against eight busy circle bots at about 105 — a fleet with nothing to do costs more than twice a fleet doing the work. That is backwards, and it is over the frame budget the benchmark now reports against: four of those ticks in one frame would be about 7.4 ms of a tablet's 16.7 ms. It is not urgent — no shoo bot ships, its debut is Q-56 — which is why the benchmark reports it beside the verdict rather than as the verdict. Find what an idle shoo bot does every tick that a working bot does not; the suspicion is that it re-picks a patrol beat or re-plans a route it then throws away, the same shape as the cost Q-67 found in the pathfinder. Whatever changes, routes must come out identical — every recorded session's walks are recomputed through this A*, and test_pathfinder_identity and the demo replay are the proof.
first_action: Run the benchmark and read _fleet_run's shoo configuration, then profile one idle shoo bot's tick against one circle bot's.
source_message: Found while deriving the benchmark's new frame-budget target: the parked fleet is the one configuration that does not fit in it.
